# help.txt — generated by tools/musil-help.py from the doc comments of Musil as Moritz uses it; do not edit
#quote
  (quote x)
  'x: x itself, unevaluated: code as data
#do
  (do forms...)
  evaluate in order, return the last; what { } builds
#if
  (if cond then [else])
  cond is true unless it is 0, nil, empty, or a vector with a zero
#while
  (while cond body)
  loop; (break) and (continue) inside it
#for
  (for init cond step body)
  C-style loop: (for (var i 0) (< i 10) (var i (+ i 1)) { ... })
#var
  (var name value)
  define name in the current environment; a function's var is always local
#set
  (set name value)
  assign to the nearest existing name, however far out; error if none
#function
  (function name (params)
  body) define a function; (function (params) body) an anonymous one
#return
  (return [value])
  leave the function; free in tail position
#break continue
  (break)  (continue)
  leave or restart the innermost loop
#try
  (try body catch e handler)
  run body; on an error bind its message to e and run handler
#expr
  (expr (a op b ...)
  ) infix arithmetic: + - * / % < > <= >= == != && ||; ( ) groups, (f x) calls
#parse
  (parse "text")
  read Musil source into a form: (do line ...), the same reading a file gets; (eval (parse s)) runs it
#eval
  (eval form)
  evaluate a form (code built as data) in the global environment
#apply
  (apply f list)
  call f with the elements of list as arguments
#+ - * /
  (+ a b ...)  (- a [b ...])  (* a b ...)  (/ a [b ...])
  arithmetic, elementwise with size-1 broadcasting;
  (- x) negates, (/ x) is the reciprocal, (+) is 0 and (*) is 1
#< > <= >=
  (< a b)  (> a b)  (<= a b)  (>= a b)
  comparisons: elementwise 1/0 on numbers, lexicographic on two strings
#== !=
  (== a b)  (!= a b)
  equality: elementwise on numbers, structural on anything else
#equal?
  (equal? a b)
  structural equality as a single 1/0, also for vectors and nested lists
#same?
  (same? a b)
  are a and b the same object (not merely equal in value)? For records and lists: the very one, however
  large; a number or a string is never the same object as another copy of it
#sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt exp log log2 log10
  (sin x)  (cos x)  (tan x)  (asin x)  (acos x)  (atan x)  (sqrt x)  (exp x)  (log x)  (log2 x)  (log10 x)
  trigonometry and logs, elementwise
#abs floor ceil round
  (abs x)  (floor x)  (ceil x)  (round x)
  rounding and magnitude, elementwise
#tanh
  (tanh x)
  hyperbolic tangent, elementwise (a soft clip for signals)
#mod pow atan2
  (mod a b)  (pow a b)  (atan2 y x)
  remainder (sign follows fmod), power, two-argument arctangent; elementwise
#not
  (not x)
  the negation of a truth value
#and or
  (and a b ...)  (or a b ...)
  short-circuit, left to right: (and) stops at the first false value, (or) at the first true one;
  the last argument is returned as it is, so (or x default) is x when x is true. Special forms: later arguments are
  not evaluated when the answer is known, so (and (> k 0) (getidx v k)) is safe.
#min max
  (min v)  (max v)
  smallest or largest element of one vector; with several arguments, elementwise over them
#list
  (list x ...)
  a list of anything
#append
  (append L x ...)
  a new list with x ... at the end
#push
  (push L x)
  append in place, returning the list; (pop L) remove and return the last element
#append
  (append L x ...)
  a new list with x ... added at the end
#pop
  (pop L)
  remove and return the last element of a list, in place
#length head tail empty?
  (length x)  (head x)  (tail x)  (empty? x)
  on a list, a vector or a string
#getidx
  (getidx x k)
  element k of a list, vector or string; negative k counts from the end
#setidx
  (setidx x k v)
  set element k of a list or vector in place
#vec
  (vec x ...)
  a vector from numbers, vectors and lists of numbers, concatenated; a scalar is a vector of size 1
#sum
  (sum v)
  sum of the elements (0 for an empty vector)
#print
  (print x ...)
  print the arguments separated by spaces, then a newline
#exit
  (exit [code])
  end the program
#type
  (type x)
  "scalar" "vec" "string" "symbol" "list" "function" "nil" or "opaque:tag"
#str
  (str x)
  x printed as a string
#sym
  (sym s)
  a symbol from a string; (num s) a number from a string
#copy
  (copy x)
  a shallow copy: a new list or vector with the same elements
#error
  (error x ...)
  raise an error with the arguments as message
#clock
  (clock)
  seconds from a monotonic clock, for timing
#load
  (load "file.mu")
  run a file once, searched next to the loading file, in the current directory,
  in MUSIL_PATH and in ~/.musil
#defined?
  (defined? 'name)
  is name bound?
#vars
  (vars)
  the global names, sorted
#help
  (help name)
  print the documentation of a builtin or library function (from help.txt)
#num
  (num s)
  the number written in a string (or a number unchanged)
#live-objects
  (live-objects)
  => (values environments): how many are alive in the whole process (tests use it to
  check that what a program makes is freed)
#range range range
  (range n)  (range a b)  (range a b step)
  a vector of evenly spaced numbers, end excluded
#seed
  (seed n)
  seed the random generator so that rand repeats
#rand
  (rand)
  a number in [0, 1); (rand n) a vector of n of them
#sort
  (sort v)
  the elements of a vector in ascending order
#argsort
  (argsort v)
  the indices that would sort a vector ascending (stable: equal values keep their order)
#reverse
  (reverse x)
  a list, vector or string reversed
#slice
  (slice x start [count])
  part of a list, vector or string; negative start counts from the end
#find
  (find x v)
  index of the first element equal to v, or of the substring v in a string; -1 if absent
#concat
  (concat x ...)
  the arguments printed and joined into one string
#get
  (get rec key)
  the value of key; an error when absent
#opt
  (opt rec key default)
  the value of key in a record, or default
#has?
  (has? rec key)
  is the key present?
#put!
  (put! rec key value)
  set a key in place (replacing an existing pair, or adding one); returns the record
#split
  (split s sep)
  the pieces of s between occurrences of sep; (split s "") the characters
#join
  (join L sep)
  the elements of L printed and joined with sep
#format
  (format "text {} more {}" x y)
  each {} replaced by the next argument
#upper lower trim
  (upper s)  (lower s)  (trim s)
  case changes and whitespace trimming
#chr
  (chr n)
  the character with code n
#ord
  (ord s)
  the code of the first character of s
#read
  (read path)
  the whole file as a string; a relative path that does not exist in the current
  directory is looked for next to the file being run (so a script finds its data from anywhere)
#write
  (write path x)
  write x (printed) to a file, replacing it
#append-file
  (append-file path x)
  write x (printed) at the end of a file
#directory?
  (directory? path)
  is the path an existing directory?
#exists?
  (exists? path)
  does the file or directory exist?
#input
  (input [prompt])
  a line read from the console, or nil at end of input
#map
  (map x f)
  f applied to every element: a list for a list; for a vector, a vector when every result is a number, a list otherwise
#filter
  (filter x f)
  the elements for which f is true, as a list or vector like x
#reduce
  (reduce x f init)
  fold: (f (f (f init x0) x1) x2) ...
#assert
  (assert cond [message ...])
  stop with an error unless cond is true
#regex-match?
  (regex-match? pattern s)
  does the regular expression (ECMAScript syntax) match anywhere in s?
#sign
  (sign x)
  -1, 0 or 1
#even? odd?
  (even? n)  (odd? n)
#between?
  (between? x lo hi)
  lo <= x <= hi
#hypot
  (hypot a b)
  sqrt(a^2 + b^2)
#gcd lcm
  (gcd a b)  (lcm a b)
  on non-negative integers
#lerp
  (lerp a b t)
  linear interpolation, t in [0, 1]
#map-range
  (map-range x in-lo in-hi out-lo out-hi)
  re-map x from one range into another
#deg->rad rad->deg
  (deg->rad d)  (rad->deg r)
#zeros
  (zeros n)
  vector of n zeros
#ones
  (ones n)
  vector of n ones
#linspace
  (linspace a b n)
  n points from a to b inclusive
#mean
  (mean v)
  arithmetic mean
#prod
  (prod v)
  product of the elements
#dot
  (dot a b)
  inner product (sizes must match)
#norm
  (norm v)
  euclidean norm
#cumsum
  (cumsum v)
  running sum
#stdev
  (stdev v)
  population standard deviation
#normalize
  (normalize v)
  scale to [0, 1]; a constant vector becomes zeros
#diff
  (diff v)
  first differences, one element shorter
#argmin argmax
  (argmin v)  (argmax v)
  index of the smallest / largest element
#median
  (median v)
  the middle value (mean of the two middle values for even length)
#quantile
  (quantile v q)
  value below which a fraction q of the data lies (linear interpolation)
#histogram
  (histogram v bins)
  counts per bin over [min v, max v]; returns (list counts edges)
#interp1
  (interp1 xs ys xq)
  linear interpolation of the table (xs, ys) at the points xq;
  xs must be increasing; xq outside the table is clamped to the ends
#clip
  (clip v lo hi)
  clamp every element to [lo, hi]
#fixed
  (fixed x d)
  round x to d decimal places
#last
  (last x)
  last element
#take
  (take x n)
  first n elements
#drop
  (drop x n)
  all but the first n elements
#vec->list
  (vec->list v)
  the elements of a vector as a list
#contains?
  (contains? x v)
  is v an element of x (or a substring, for strings)?
#each
  (each x f)
  call f on every element, for side effects; returns nil
#any?
  (any? x f)
  does f hold for some element?
#all?
  (all? x f)
  does f hold for every element?
#count
  (count x f)
  number of elements for which f holds
#concat-list
  (concat-list a b)
  a new list with the elements of a then those of b
#flatten
  (flatten L)
  one level of nested lists removed
#zip
  (zip a b)
  list of two-element lists
#unique
  (unique L)
  elements in first-seen order, duplicates removed
#sort-list
  (sort-list L)
  sort a list of numbers or strings (insertion sort; fine for short lists)
#min-of max-of
  (min-of L)  (max-of L)
  smallest / largest element of a list of numbers
#repeat
  (repeat s n)
  string s repeated n times
#starts-with? ends-with?
  (starts-with? s prefix)  (ends-with? s suffix)
#replace
  (replace s old new)
  every occurrence of old replaced by new
#count-substr
  (count-substr s pat)
  number of non-overlapping occurrences of pat
#pad-left pad-right
  (pad-left s w ch)  (pad-right s w ch)
  pad to width w with character ch
#fmt-fixed
  (fmt-fixed x d)
  x as a string with exactly d decimals: (fmt-fixed pi 4) => "3.1416"
#fmt-pct
  (fmt-pct x d)
  x as a percentage string: (fmt-pct 0.752 1) => "75.2%"
#put
  (put rec key value)
  a new record with the key set, the original untouched
#keys values
  (keys rec)  (values rec)
  the keys, the values, in order
#record
  (record key value ...)
  a record from alternating keys and values: (record 'freq 440 'dur 0.5)
#sort-by
  (sort-by L f)
  the elements ordered by f (a number or string per element), stable
#group-by
  (group-by L f)
  a record from key to the list of elements with that key, in first-seen order
#find-first
  (find-first L f)
  the first element for which f holds, or nil
#reject
  (reject L f)
  the elements for which f does not hold
#min-by max-by
  (min-by L f)  (max-by L f)
  the element with the smallest / largest f
#sum-by
  (sum-by L f)
  the sum of f over the elements
#partition
  (partition L f)
  (list those-for-which-f-holds the-others)
#remove-at insert-at
  (remove-at L k)  (insert-at L k x)
  a new list without / with an element at k
#shuffle
  (shuffle L)
  the elements in a random order (a new list)
#identity
  (identity x)
#compose
  (compose f g)
  the function x -> (f (g x))
#times
  (times n f)
  call f n times with 0 .. n-1
#assert-near
  (assert-near a b eps msg)
  numeric comparison within eps
#assert-equal
  (assert-equal actual expected msg)
  structural comparison with a helpful message
#platform
  (platform)
  => "macos", "linux" or "windows"
#exec
  (exec "command")
  => the command's standard output as a string
#getenv
  (getenv "NAME")
  => value or nil
#sleep
  (sleep seconds)
#find-file
  (find-file "name")
  => the path of a file as load resolves it (the current directory, the file being run, the
  load path: MUSIL_PATH, ~/.musil, the libraries), or "" when not found
#resolve-path
  (resolve-path "name")
  => the path a reading function would open for a relative name: as given if it exists from the
  current directory, else next to the file being run, else next to the program that was started
#interactive?
  (interactive?)
  => is the standard input a terminal? (a script asks before prompting for input)
#breathe
  (breathe)
  let the background work run once (windows, schedulers, the score player): for a long computation
  done from a window's button, once per step
#now
  (now)
  => seconds since the Unix epoch (wall clock; clock is the monotonic one)
#cwd
  (cwd)
  => current directory
#ls
  (ls [dir])
  => list of entry names, sorted
#mkdir
  (mkdir path)
  => creates the directory and its parents; nil
#remove
  (remove path)
  => deletes a file or an empty directory; 1 if something was removed
#stat
  (stat path)
  => (list size is-dir modified-seconds) or nil if it does not exist
#read-csv
  (read-csv path)
  => table. write-csv is in system.mu.
#read-wav
  (read-wav path)
  => (list sample-rate (list channel-vector ...)): 8, 16, 24 and 32-bit PCM or 32/64-bit float, any channels and rate
#write-wav
  (write-wav path sample-rate channels [bits])
  => nil. channels: a vector (mono) or a list of vectors (any number);
  bits 8, 16 (default), 24 or 32 for integer PCM, "float" (or 32.0 with a decimal point: use "float") for 32-bit IEEE
  float, "double" for 64-bit; any sample rate. Integer files clip at +-1.
#udp-send
  (udp-send host port payload [osc?])
  => 1 on success, 0 on failure. With osc?=1 the payload is
#udp-receive
  (udp-receive host port [timeout-seconds])
  => the next datagram as a string, or nil on timeout/failure
#serve
  (serve port)
  start the evaluation port; (serve-stop); (serving) => the port or 0
#file-lines
  (file-lines path)
  list of lines, without the trailing newline

  write a list of lines, one per line

  existence tests by kind
#file-size
  (file-size path)
  size in bytes, or nil
#basename dirname extension
  (basename path)  (dirname path)  (extension path)
  string surgery on paths
#csv-escape
  (csv-escape s)
  quote a field if it holds a comma, a quote or a newline
#write-csv
  (write-csv path table)
  table is a list of rows, a row a list of cells
#elapsed
  (elapsed thunk)

#wav-duration

#mat-mul
  (mat-mul A B ...)
  matrix product, left to right
#transpose
  (transpose M)
#det
  (det M)
#nmf
  (nmf V k iterations)
  => (list W H): V (r x c, non-negative) ~ W H with W r x k and H k x c, both
  non-negative, by Lee & Seung's multiplicative updates for the KL divergence (the usual choice for
  magnitude spectrograms; scientific/nmf.h, the factorisation of Moritz's nmf box). Columns of W are the
  parts (spectral shapes, of unit sum), rows of H their activations over time (the scale is in H)
#nmf-with-parts
  (nmf-with-parts V W iterations)
  => H: the activations of known parts W (its columns), V ~ W H with W
  fixed: supervised NMF, when the parts were learnt from examples of each source
#rank
  (rank M)
#inv
  (inv M)
  by Gauss-Jordan on [M | I]
#solve
  (solve A b)
  => x with A x = b
#mp
  (mp x D iterations threshold options)
  => a record: atoms (the indices of the chosen rows of D, in the order chosen),
  weights, residual, error (the residual's norm over x's), and approx (the reconstruction). x a vector, D a
  dictionary (a matrix: one atom per row, the same length as x). Greedy: the atom most correlated with the
  residual is taken with its projection weight and subtracted, until iterations are done, the error is below
  threshold, or no atom helps. options: a record with 'nonneg (1: only atoms with a positive projection, weights
  kept positive; the choice for magnitude spectra) and 'orthogonal (1: orthogonal matching pursuit, every weight
  refitted by least squares after each pick)
#median-filter
  (median-filter v order)
  the running median of width order
#eig-sym
  (eig-sym M)
  => (list eigenvalues eigenvectors) of a symmetric matrix by Jacobi rotations;
#kmeans
  (kmeans M k)
  => (list labels centroids): labels is a vector of cluster indices, centroids a k x d matrix.
  k-means++ starts and Lloyd's iterations, ten starts, the tightest kept (the same as Moritz's kmeans box)
#knn
  (knn training k queries)
  => list of predicted labels.

#fft
  (fft signal)
  => (list re im), each of length next-pow2(length); the signal is zero-padded
#ifft
  (ifft (list re im)
  ) => real signal of the same length (a power of two)
#osc
  (osc sr freqs table)
  => one sample per element of freqs, reading the wavetable with linear
#iir
  (iir x b a)
  => y with a0 y[n] = sum b[k] x[n-k] - sum a[k>0] y[n-k]; a[0] need not be 1
#delay
  (delay x d)
  => x delayed by d samples (fractional, linear interpolation), same length
#resample
  (resample x factor)
  => x with its length multiplied by factor, by windowed-sinc interpolation
#autocorr
  (autocorr x)
  => biased autocorrelation (sum / n) for lags 0 .. n/2 - 1; it decays with lag, which
#interleave
  (interleave (list a b ...)
  ) => one vector a0 b0 a1 b1 ...
#deinterleave
  (deinterleave v channels)
  => (list a b ...): the channels of an interleaved vector
#local-maxima
  (local-maxima v)
  => indices k with v[k] > v[k-1] and v[k] > v[k+1] (interior points only)
#gather
  (gather v indices)
  => the elements of v at the given (integer) indices, as a vector
#add-at!
  (add-at! dst pos src)
  => dst, with src added in place starting at pos; dst must be long enough.
#comb
  (comb x d g)
  => feedback comb y[n] = x[n] + g y[n-d]; (allpass x d g) => Schroeder allpass
#pvoc
  (pvoc x opts)
  sparkle's phase vocoder (signals/vocoder.h, the engine of Moritz's sparkle~) over
#deconv
  (deconv y h [threshold])
  => x such that (conv x h) ~ y, as long as y: the spectrum of y divided by that
  of h where |H| is above threshold (0.001) times its peak, else 0 (signals/convolution.h, as Moritz's
  condec): a recording un-reverberated by a measured response, or a response measured from a known sweep
#svf
  (svf x sr freq q type)
  => x through a state-variable filter (signals/filters.h, as Moritz's svf~);
  type is "low" "high" "band" or "notch"; q in 0..1 is the resonance; freq and q are numbers or vectors
  as long as x (a moving filter). Streams in a synth (freq and q read once per block there).
#nebula
  (nebula sr seconds opts)
  => (list left right): a cloud of grains (signals/nebula.h, the engine of
#adsr
  (adsr sr gate a d s r)
  => an envelope following a gate signal (1 = on, 0 = off): attack a and
#lag
  (lag x sr seconds)
  => x smoothed by a one-pole lowpass with the given time constant (parameter
#hpss
  (hpss x n hop kernel)
  => (list harmonic percussive): STFT with a periodic Hann window of n and
#ambi-gains
  (ambi-gains order az el)
  => the (order+1)^2 encoding gains (SN3D, ACN) of a direction
#ambi-decoder
  (ambi-decoder order speakers)
  => the decoding matrix ambi-decode uses: a row of (order+1)^2 gains per speaker
  (speakers: (list az el) or azimuths). All at ear height: a ring, the exact horizontal decoder with 2D max-rE
  weights; with elevations: sampling of the sphere, SN3D-corrected (2n+1) with 3D max-rE weights
#ambi-rotate
  (ambi-rotate B yaw)
  => B turned by yaw degrees about the vertical axis (positive to the left):
  within each order, the pair (m, -m) rotates by m yaw, exactly; B is a list of (order+1)^2 channel vectors
#conv-fast
  (conv-fast x h)
  => the linear convolution of x and h (length n + m - 1), by overlap-add over blocks the size
  of h: the same result as conv, faster on long inputs, and the interpreter breathes between blocks (the
  windows stay responsive while a long score goes through the hall)
#hrtf-load
  (hrtf-load path)
  load a set from a CSV: each row azimuth, elevation, then the left ear's samples and the right's
  (as src/hrtf_kemar.csv, the MIT KEMAR compact set at 44100 Hz, found on the load path); => the number of directions.
  Once a set is loaded, hrir takes the nearest measured direction (resampled to the requested rate);
  (hrtf-unload) goes back to the spherical-head model; (hrtf-loaded) => directions loaded, 0 for the model.
#hrir-model
  (hrir-model az el sr)
  => the spherical-head model, whatever is loaded (below)
#hrir
  (hrir az el sr)
  => (list left right): the nearest measured direction of the loaded set (the MIT KEMAR set is loaded
  from the load path on first use), resampled to sr; the spherical-head model when no set is available
  for each ear a head-shadow filter, whose high-frequency roll-off grows with the angle from that ear, and the
  interaural delay (Woodworth). No measured data: the model externalises and lateralises well enough to work with;
  real HRTFs can replace it (a WAV pair per direction convolved the same way).
#binaural-level
  (binaural-level sr speakers)
  => the gain that gives a front source, decoded at order 1 to these virtual speakers
  (ambi-decoder) and rendered with their head responses (hrir), the energy of the front head response itself;
  binaural-decode uses it (it depends on the rate and on the set of responses loaded)
#chromagram
  (chromagram x sr n hop)
  => a 12 x frames matrix (rows C C# D ... B), a frame every hop samples, the first at 0.
  Read from the spectral peaks (as HPCP) of the magnitude spectrogram (Hann n): the local maxima above -80 dB and
  above 1/1000 of the frame's strongest, their frequency refined by a parabola through the peak and its
  neighbours (on the log magnitudes), each given to the pitch class of its nearest note between C2 and B6, so a
  tone counts once; a peak that is probably the 3rd, 5th, 6th or 7th partial of a lower one (at that fraction of
  its frequency within a third of a semitone, and at least 0.3 as loud) counts a tenth, so overtones do not pull
  the harmony a fifth or a third up. Every frame scaled to a maximum of 1 (a silent frame stays 0)
#self-similarity
  (self-similarity F)
  => the frames x frames matrix of the cosine similarity between the columns of a feature
  matrix F (rows are features, columns frames: a chromagram, a spectrogram); 1 on the diagonal, 0 for frames
  with nothing in common (Foote 1999: the structure of a piece as a picture, repeats as stripes off the diagonal)
#foote-novelty
  (foote-novelty S width)
  => a vector, one value per frame: the self-similarity matrix correlated along its
  diagonal with a checkerboard kernel of width x width (Gaussian-tapered; width even, ~16-64 frames): the mean
  similarity within the past and within the future minus the mean similarity between them, each weighted by the
  kernel and taken only over what lies inside the matrix (0 near the ends, where less than half of the kernel
  fits). High where what comes before is unlike what comes after, the boundaries of the sections (Foote 2000)
#tempogram
  (tempogram flux fps window [step])
  => a matrix bpm x columns: every step frames (1 by default: a column per frame;
  (/ fps 4) gives four columns a second, much faster on a long piece), the autocorrelation of the onset strength
  (a vector, fps values a second) over a Hann window of window frames around the frame, read at the lags of the
  tempi 30..300 bpm (one row per bpm; a lag between two frames interpolated; only the lags of that range are
  computed). The strength is first taken above its local mean (0.3 s) and rectified: its peaks, without the slow
  decay of a big hit, which would look periodic at every tempo. Every column is divided by the autocorrelation at
  lag 0 (the window's energy), so 1 is a perfectly periodic pulse and a passage without one stays dark
#beat-track
  (beat-track flux fps bpm tightness)
  => the frames of the beats (a vector): dynamic programming over the onset
  strength (fps values a second) for the sequence of beats that is strong and keeps near the period of bpm
  (tightness, ~100: how much a deviation from the period costs, on a log scale; Ellis 2007)
#mel-spectrogram
  (mel-spectrogram x sr n hop nmel)
  => an nmel x frames matrix: the energy in dB of the magnitude spectrogram (Hann
  n, hop, a frame every hop samples, scaled so that a full-scale sine is 0 dB) through nmel triangular filters
  evenly spaced on the mel scale from 0 to sr/2 (a band narrower than a bin takes its nearest bin), floored at
  -100 dB for silence: a spectrogram at the ear's resolution, the timbre of every frame
#mfcc-gram
  (mfcc-gram x sr n hop nmel ncoeff)
  => an ncoeff x frames matrix: the mel-frequency cepstral coefficients of every
  frame (the DCT-II of the mel spectrogram in dB, nmel filters, the first ncoeff coefficients: a smooth description of
  the spectral envelope, the timbre; coefficient 0 is the overall level)
#sine
  (sine sr freq dur)
  a sine of freq Hz lasting dur seconds
#noise
  (noise n)
  white noise in [-1, 1]; n may also be a signal, giving noise of its length
  (so an instrument can write (noise gate): offline as long as the gate, streamed forever)
#impulse
  (impulse n)
  a 1 followed by n-1 zeros
#gen
  (gen n amps)
  one period of a wavetable with the given harmonic amplitudes, plus a
  guard point (n+1 samples, last = first), normalised to a peak of 1; for osc
#oscbank
  (oscbank sr amps freqs table)
  sum of oscillators; amps and freqs are lists of per-sample envelopes
#mix
  (mix layers)
  overlay (list (list position signal) ...) into one signal
#add-at
  (add-at dst pos src)
  dst with src added starting at pos; dst grows if needed
#pan
  (pan x pos)
  a mono signal to (list left right), equal power; pos from -1 (left) to 1 (right)
#fade-in fade-out
  (fade-in x n)  (fade-out x n)
  linear fades over n samples
#rms
  (rms x)
  root mean square
#normalize-peak
  (normalize-peak x)
  scale so the peak is 1; (normalize-rms x target) so the rms is target
#normalize-rms
  (normalize-rms x target)
  scale so the rms is target
#amp->db db->amp
  (amp->db x)  (db->amp d)
  amplitude to decibels and back
#next-pow2
  (next-pow2 n)
  the smallest power of two >= n (fft sizes)
#window
  (window n a0 a1 a2)
  generalised cosine window, periodic (so hann overlap-adds exactly at hop n/4);
  (hann n) (hamming n) (blackman n) are the usual ones
#hann hamming blackman
  (hann n)  (hamming n)  (blackman n)
  the usual windows, periodic
#hamming
  (hamming n)
  the Hamming window
#blackman
  (blackman n)
  the Blackman window
#car->pol
  (car->pol spec)
  (list re im) -> (list mag phase); (pol->car) the other way
#pol->car
  (pol->car spec)
  (list mag phase) -> (list re im)
#magnitudes phases
  (magnitudes spec)  (phases spec)
  from a complex spectrum
#spectrum-freqs
  (spectrum-freqs n sr)
  the frequency of each of the first n/2 bins
#magnitude-spectrum
  (magnitude-spectrum x)
  the positive-frequency magnitudes of x, normalised so a full-scale sine reads 1
#complex-mul
  (complex-mul a b)
  product of two (list re im) spectra
#conv
  (conv x h)
  linear convolution through the FFT, length (+ (length x) (length h) -1)
#cepstrum
  (cepstrum mags)
  real cepstrum of a full (symmetric) magnitude spectrum
#spectral-envelope
  (spectral-envelope mags order)
  smooth envelope of a full magnitude spectrum: the "true envelope",
  a cepstral smoothing (first `order` coefficients) iterated so that it rides
  on the harmonic peaks instead of averaging peaks and valleys. The order sets
  the resolution: about sr / (2 f0) of the sound (e.g. 150 for a voice at
  44.1 kHz) follows the formants without rippling at the harmonics
#flatten-spectrum
  (flatten-spectrum mags order)
  the magnitudes divided by their envelope: the fine structure alone
#impose-envelope
  (impose-envelope mags source order)
  mags reshaped to carry the spectral envelope of source
#stft
  (stft x n hop)
  => list of (list re im); (istft frames n hop) => signal by overlap-add
#istft
  (istft frames n hop)
  the signal back from stft frames by windowed overlap-add
#stft-magnitudes
  (stft-magnitudes frames)
  list of positive-frequency magnitude vectors, one per frame
#princarg
  (princarg x)
  wrap a phase to (-pi, pi]
#ramp
  (ramp v)
  a parameter given as a number or as (list start end) -> (list start end)
#fftshift
  (fftshift v)
  rotate a vector by half its length (zero-phase windowing)
#pvoc-stretch
  (pvoc-stretch x factor)
  time-stretch by factor with the pitch kept
#pvoc-pitch
  (pvoc-pitch x ratio)
  pitch-shift by ratio at the same length (formants move too)
#pvoc-pitch-formant
  (pvoc-pitch-formant x ratio order)
  pitch-shift keeping the formants (order about sr/100: 400 at 44.1 kHz)
#pvoc-formants
  (pvoc-formants x ratio order)
  move the formants by ratio, the pitch kept
#pvoc-cross
  (pvoc-cross x y mode amount order)
  cross synthesis of x by y: mode 1 multiplicative,
  2 spectral flattener (y's envelope on x), 3 morphing
#robotize
  (robotize x)
  zero phases: a buzz at the frame rate
#whisperize
  (whisperize x)
  random phases: the spectral envelope on noise
#denoise
  (denoise x threshold)
  magnitudes below threshold x the peak are zeroed (0.01 - 0.1)
#gate-spectrum
  (gate-spectrum mags threshold)
  magnitudes below threshold times the frame's peak set to zero
#spectral-morph
  (spectral-morph a b t n hop)
  between two sounds of the same length: magnitudes interpolated
  linearly, phases taken from a below t = 0.5 and from b above
#onset-strength
  (onset-strength x n hop)
  the spectral flux of every frame, as a vector (one value per hop)
#onsets
  (onsets x sr n hop threshold)
  onset times in seconds, always starting with 0 (so the segments cover the
  sound from its beginning): then the peaks of the spectral flux (local maxima) above
  threshold x the flux's maximum, at least n samples apart from the previous onset, each
  placed at the sample where the energy jumps inside its frame (64-sample blocks: the
  block with the largest rise), so a hit is found where it starts, not a window early
#onsets-adaptive
  (onsets-adaptive x sr n hop threshold width)
  the same with a threshold that follows the material: a peak
  counts when it exceeds threshold x the moving median of the flux over width frames
  (odd, e.g. 9); for sounds whose loudness drifts, where a global level misses the
  quiet hits or admits the loud sustain
#onsets-of-flux
  (onsets-of-flux x sr n hop flux level)
  the shared picker: peaks of flux above level (a vector), spaced and refined
#onset-refine
  (onset-refine x start n)
  the sample within [start, start + n) where the energy rises most (64-sample blocks)
#segments
  (segments x sr times)
  the pieces of x between consecutive onset times (and the end), as a list
#spectral-moment
  (spectral-moment amps freqs order centroid)
  weighted moment of the frequencies about a centroid
#spectral-centroid
  (spectral-centroid amps freqs)
  amplitude-weighted mean frequency
#spectral-spread
  (spectral-spread amps freqs)
  standard deviation around the centroid
#spectral-skewness
  (spectral-skewness amps freqs)
  asymmetry of the spectrum about its centroid
#spectral-kurtosis
  (spectral-kurtosis amps freqs)
  peakedness of the spectrum about its centroid
#spectral-flux
  (spectral-flux amps previous)
  rectified increase from the previous frame
#spectral-irregularity
  (spectral-irregularity amps)
  sum of absolute differences between neighbouring bins
#spectral-decrease
  (spectral-decrease amps)
  weighted decrease relative to the first bin
#spectral-flatness
  (spectral-flatness amps)
  geometric over arithmetic mean: 1 for noise, 0 for a pure tone
#spectral-rolloff
  (spectral-rolloff amps freqs fraction)
  frequency below which the fraction of the energy lies
#hfc
  (hfc amps)
  high-frequency content
#zcr
  (zcr x)
  zero-crossing rate per sample
#acf-f0
  (acf-f0 x sr)
  fundamental by autocorrelation; 0 when no clear peak
#biquad
  (biquad type sr f0 q gain-db)
  => (list b a) of an RBJ biquad; type is one of
  "lowpass" "highpass" "bandpass" "notch" "peak" "lowshelf" "highshelf"
#apply-filter
  (apply-filter x coeffs)
  run x through (list b a) as returned by biquad
#lowpass highpass bandpass notch
  (lowpass x sr f0 q)  (highpass x sr f0 q)  (bandpass x sr f0 q)  (notch x sr f0 q)
  one biquad, applied
#lores
  (lores x sr cutoff res)
  a resonant lowpass, res 0..1 (the biquad of Moritz's lores~: q = 0.707 + 24 res^2)
#highpass
  (highpass x sr f0 q)
  a highpass biquad, applied
#bandpass
  (bandpass x sr f0 q)
  a bandpass biquad, applied
#notch
  (notch x sr f0 q)
  a notch biquad, applied
#peak-eq lowshelf highshelf
  (peak-eq x sr f0 q gain-db)  (lowshelf x sr f0 q gain-db)  (highshelf x sr f0 q gain-db)
  the equaliser biquads, applied
#lowshelf
  (lowshelf x sr f0 q gain-db)
  a low shelf, applied
#highshelf
  (highshelf x sr f0 q gain-db)
  a high shelf, applied
#dc-block
  (dc-block x)
  remove the DC offset; (dc-block-r x r) with pole radius r (default 0.995)
#dc-block-r
  (dc-block-r x r)
  a DC blocker with pole radius r
#reson
  (reson x sr freq tau)
  two-pole resonator at freq Hz with decay time tau seconds; the output
  lasts tau seconds, so a short excitation rings out
#schroeder-reverb
  (schroeder-reverb x sr rt60)
  four parallel combs into two allpasses; rt60 is the decay time in
  seconds (how long the tail takes to fall by 60 dB). The output is the input
  plus rt60 seconds, so the tail is not cut off.
#resample-to
  (resample-to x sr-in sr-out)
#bpf
  (bpf start segments)
  break-point function: piecewise linear segments as one vector; segments is a
  list of (list length end): (bpf 0 (list (list 4 1) (list 4 0))) rises then falls.
  Each segment's end value is excluded (it starts the next one).
#envelope-follow
  (envelope-follow x n)
  rms over hops of n samples, one value per hop
#envelope-from-values
  (envelope-from-values v hop)
  piecewise-linear signal through successive values, hop samples apart
#frame-spectra
  (frame-spectra x block hop ncoeff)
  the magnitude spectrum of every frame (a Hann window of block samples every
  hop), the first ncoeff bins: the same space as a database's spectrum features, one
  spectrum per frame instead of the average
#spectral-similarity
  (spectral-similarity a b)
  the cosine similarity of two magnitude spectra on a log scale (1: alike; 0: unrelated)
#event-rate
  (event-rate x sr window hop)
  how many attacks a second around every instant: the peaks of the spectral flux
  that stand above its moving median (twice it, at least 60 ms apart: a held
  sound's tremolo or vibrato ripples at the floor and does not count), counted in a
  window of window seconds, one value every hop samples; => (list times rates peaks)
#flux-peaks
  (flux-peaks x sr n hop threshold width)
  the times (seconds) of the peaks of the spectral flux (the rectified change
  of the magnitude spectrum, n and hop as onset-strength) that stand above threshold times the
  flux's moving median over width frames (odd): every noticeable spectral change, an attack or
  not, counted as the target's activity; threshold 2 keeps the attacks, 1.5 admits the ripples
  of a held sound too; peaks within 50 ms of the previous one count as one; => a vector
#peak-density
  (peak-density times secs window hop)
  how many of some times (a vector, seconds) fall a second around every instant:
  the count within window seconds centred on each hop-second step over secs seconds, divided by
  the window; => a vector, one value per step (a density in events a second)
#polyphony-estimate
  (polyphony-estimate spectra)
  how many voices seem to sound in each frame: the spectral peaks above 15% of the
  frame's strongest, about three strong partials a voice (1..16); 0 for a frame below -60 dB
  (spectra of block/2 bins, as frame-spectra gives, a full-scale sine peaking near block/4).
  A rough estimate, not a transcription; smooth it with median-filter; => a vector, one per frame
#register-curve
  (register-curve spectra sr block)
  where the sound sits: for each frame the centroid in MIDI pitch (the powers
  weighting the pitch of every bin above 30 Hz, so an octave is an octave), the spread around
  it in octaves, and the lowest strong partial in MIDI pitch (a tone's fundamental, more or
  less: where the register begins). A frame below -60 dB (its peak under 1/1000 of a
  full-scale sine's, block/4) keeps the values of the frame before (60, 1 and 48 at the
  start), so quiet noise does not make the curves jump; smooth them with median-filter;
  => (list centroids spreads lows)
#loudness-curve
  (loudness-curve x sr hop)
  the level of every hop in dB, roughly as the ear weighs it (the extreme bass and treble
  taken out); => a vector, one value per hop, -100 for silence
#coherence-time
  (coherence-time spectra hop sr threshold)
  how long the sound keeps its spectrum from each frame on: the time until
  the spectral-similarity with the frame falls under threshold (0.75 is reasonable), at most
  8 s; a sustained sound gives long times, a percussive one short; => a vector
#spectral-peaks
  (spectral-peaks m sr block n)
  the n strongest peaks of a magnitude spectrum as (list freqs mags), each frequency
  refined by a parabola through the peak and its neighbours
#converb
  (converb x ir dry wet)
  x through an impulse response: x a vector or a list of channels, ir a vector (applied to every
  channel) or a list of channels (one per output channel; a mono x is spread over them); => a
  list of channels, dry x plus wet x convolved, as long as x plus the response's tail
#hall-ir
  (hall-ir sr)
  the impulse response of the Concertgebouw (Amsterdam), shipped with the libraries, at a rate
#concerthall
  (concerthall x sr dry wet)
  x (a vector or channels, at sr) in the Concertgebouw: converb with the shipped response;
  => stereo (a mono x is placed in the middle), as long as x plus the hall's tail (~3 s)
#pan-azimuth
  (pan-azimuth x az)
  a mono signal to (list left right), equal power from its azimuth (-90 right .. 90 left;
  behind is folded onto the front)
#speaker-ring
  (speaker-ring n)
  n speakers evenly around, as azimuths starting in front and going left
#pan-n
  (pan-n x speakers az)
  a mono signal onto a horizontal ring of speakers (a list of azimuths) by amplitude
  panning between the two nearest speakers (VBAP in 2D); => a list of n channels
#princarg-deg
  (princarg-deg a)
  an angle wrapped to -180..180
#ambi-encode
  (ambi-encode x order az el)
  a mono signal at a direction as B-format: (order+1)^2 channels (ACN, SN3D)
#ambi-add
  (ambi-add a b)
  two B-format signals of the same order summed
#ambi-decode
  (ambi-decode B speakers)
  B-format to a list of speakers, each (list az el) or a bare azimuth, through the
  matrix of ambi-decoder: for speakers all at ear height the exact horizontal decoder of a
  ring (at least 2N+1 speakers, evenly spaced) with 2D max-rE weights, whose energy vector
  reaches 0.71 at order 1 and 0.87 at order 2; with elevations, sampling of the sphere with
  the SN3D correction (2n+1) and 3D max-rE weights
#max-re-weights
  (max-re-weights order)
  the per-channel 2D max-rE weights of an order (Zotter & Frank), cos(n pi / (2N + 2)) for
  the channels of order n: they concentrate the energy vector of a ring decoder (ambi-decoder)
#binaural
  (binaural x az el sr)
  a mono signal at a direction for headphones: convolved with the two ears' impulse
  responses of a spherical head (hrir); => (list left right)
#channel
  (channel sig k)
  one channel of a multichannel signal (a list of vectors); a vector is its own channel
#stereo-add stereo-scale
  (stereo-add a b)  (stereo-scale a g)
  stereo signals summed, scaled (written with channel, so they stream)
#binaural-decode
  (binaural-decode B sr)
  B-format for headphones: decoded to 17 virtual speakers spread over the sphere (8 at ear
  height, 4 above, 4 below, 1 overhead, the sphere-sampling decoder of ambi-decoder), each
  rendered with the head responses of its direction (hrir), summed; at order 1 a front
  source has the broadband level of the front head response itself (low frequencies come out
  louder, high ones softer, as with any decoding to virtual speakers); => (list left right). One expression, so it streams in a synth too.
#normalize-peak-stereo
  (normalize-peak-stereo s)
  a stereo (or any multichannel) signal scaled so its loudest sample is 1
#ambi-render
  (ambi-render sources order)
  several (list x az el) placed and summed as one B-format signal
#moving-source
  (moving-source x order az-curve el-curve blocks)
  a signal whose direction changes: encoded block by block
  (blocks samples each) at the azimuth and elevation curves (vectors, one value per block)
#nmf-separate
  (nmf-separate x n hop k iterations)
  x split into k sources: NMF of its magnitude spectrogram
  (V = magnitudes, bins x frames) into k parts, then a Wiener mask per part
  (its share of W H at every bin and frame) applied to the complex spectra
  and inverted; => (list (list source-1 ... source-k) W H). The sources add
  up to the input. Which part is which sound is for the caller to decide
  (their spectral shapes W and activations H say).
#nmf-spectrogram
  (nmf-spectrogram frames n)
  the magnitude spectrogram of stft frames as a bins x frames matrix
#nmf-sources
  (nmf-sources x frames n hop W H groups)
  the sources of a factorization: groups is a list of lists of part
  indices, one source per group (a source may be several parts); Wiener masks, ISTFT
#nmf-learn-parts
  (nmf-learn-parts examples n hop k iterations)
  supervised separation, step one: for each example sound
  (a list of vectors, one per source) learn k spectral parts by NMF; => W with
  k columns per source, and the groups (which columns belong to which source)
#nmf-separate-with
  (nmf-separate-with x n hop W groups iterations)
  supervised separation, step two: the mix x against known
  parts W (nmf-with-parts learns only the activations), one source per group
#chroma-mean
  (chroma-mean C)
  the pitch-class distribution of a chromagram: its rows averaged over time; => a vector of 12
#rotate-vec
  (rotate-vec v k)
  the vector rotated right by k (v[0] goes to position k)
#key-scores
  (key-scores chroma)
  every key against a pitch-class distribution (a vector of 12, C first: chroma-mean of a
  chromagram): the correlation of the distribution with the Krumhansl-Kessler profile of each
  major and minor key (Krumhansl 1990); => (list (list "D" 'minor r) ...), best first
#correlation
  (correlation a b)
  Pearson's correlation of two vectors
#key-estimate
  (key-estimate chroma)
  the best of key-scores: (list "D" 'minor r)
#key-name
  (key-name k)
  "D minor" from a key-scores entry
#tempo-estimate
  (tempo-estimate flux fps)
  the tempo of an onset strength (a vector, fps values a second): the autocorrelation
  of the flux read at the lags of 30..300 bpm, weighted by a log-normal prior on the tempo a
  listener taps, centred on 100 bpm and 0.6 octaves wide (the pulse of the eighths or the
  bars is often as periodic as the beat's: the prior decides between the octaves); => bpm
#tempo-estimate-with
  (tempo-estimate-with flux fps centre width)
  the same with the prior's centre (bpm) and width (octaves) given;
  (tempo-estimate-with flux fps 120 10) is the autocorrelation's own peak
#beats
  (beats x sr n hop)
  the beat times of a recording in seconds: the onset strength (n, hop as onset-strength),
  its tempo (tempo-estimate) and the beats tracked on it (beat-track, tightness 100); a
  frame's time is the middle of its window (the flux rises when an attack enters it);
  => (list bpm times)
#clicks
  (clicks times sr seconds)
  a signal of seconds seconds with a short click at each of the times (a vector): to hear
  the beats found over the recording ((+ x (clicks ...)) or in the other channel)
#beat-sync
  (beat-sync M times fps)
  a feature matrix (rows features, columns frames at fps) averaged between successive beat
  times (seconds): one column per beat; the chromagram of a song in a few hundred columns
  (a self-similarity matrix on it shows the form at the scale of the beat)
#novelty-peaks
  (novelty-peaks nov fps threshold width)
  the times (seconds) of the peaks of a novelty curve (foote-novelty)
  standing above threshold times its moving median over width frames (odd), at least a
  second apart; the boundaries of the sections; => a vector
#mat-log1p
  (mat-log1p M scale)
  log(1 + scale x) of every element: a spectrogram or a similarity matrix for an image
#pitch->midi
  (pitch->midi "D#5")
  => 75: a note name with sharps (#, _) or flats (b) and an octave (C4 = 60); -1 if not a pitch
#midi->pitch
  (midi->pitch 75)
  => "D#5"
#db-read
  (db-read path)
  => (list type block hop ncoeff entries): the feature file parsed; each entry a record
  (file instr tech pitch dyn other midi features), the file relative to the database's root
#db-gen
  (db-gen folder path type block hop ncoeff)
  => the number of sounds analysed: every WAV under folder (recursively), its
  features written to path in the database format (first line: type block hop ncoeff; then the file's path
  relative to folder and the features); the file names carry the metadata (instr-tech-pitch-dyn-other).
  Sounds that cannot be read are skipped with a message.
#db-locate
  (db-locate root file)
  => the path on disk of a sound named file (a path from a feature file) under root, found by its
  file name whatever the folders are called; "" when it is not there. (db-index-size root) => how many sounds root holds
#orchidea-analyse
  (orchidea-analyse x sr type block hop ncoeff opts)
  the target's segments for a mimetic orchestration: x a vector at
  sr (resampled to 44100 Hz, the databases' rate), cut at its onsets, each segment analysed into the features of the
  database's type (block, hop, ncoeff, as db-gen makes them) and standardised, and into the pitches of its partials
  with their cents. opts a record: 'segmentation ("flux": the onsets of the spectral flux above 'threshold, a
  'timegate apart; "frames": every block; "none": one segment; or a list of onset times in seconds), 'threshold
  (2: above 1 there is one segment, a static target), 'timegate (0.1 s), 'partials-window (32768), 'partials
  (0.2: the threshold on the partials, 0..1, 0 for no pitch filter), 'extra-pitches (names added to every segment)
  => a list of records (at dur features notes), notes a record from pitch name to cents
#orchidea-search
  (orchidea-search entries orchestra segments opts)
  Orchidea's genetic search: entries a database's entries (records
  with instr tech pitch dyn other features), orchestra a list of players as strings ("Fl", "Fl|Picc"), segments as
  orchidea-analyse gives them, opts a record: 'population 'epochs 'pursuit 'crossover 'mutation 'sparsity 'positive
  'negative 'hysteresis 'regularization 'dovetail 'movement 'solutions (the best kept per segment) 'connection
  ("closest", "best" or "path") 'octaves (the pitch filter widened by octaves) 'styles 'dynamics 'others (lists of
  names that filter the search space) 'seed 'quiet
  => a record: 'segments a list, one per segment, each a record ('solutions (list (list cost (list index...)) ...),
  the best first, an index -1 for a silent player; 'curve the fitness per epoch; 'players the index in the
  orchestra of each of the solution's slots: the players that had sounds in the search space; 'missing the target's
  pitches no sound of the orchestra covers; 'used how many players the chosen solution sounds; 'held how many hold
  their sound on from the segment before ('sustain 1: a player whose pitch the target keeps is not searched again,
  for at most 'hold seconds); 'space the sounds in the search space), 'choices the connection's solution per
  segment, 'cache the fitness cache's hits and misses; 'patience (150) stops a search that stalls
#maple-gabor
  (maple-gabor sr [lo hi fmax])
  a dictionary of Gabor atoms (Gaussian-windowed cosines) for sounds at rate sr: every
  window length from lo to hi samples (powers of 2; 256 and 8192), every frequency up to fmax (16000), every position
#maple-gammatone
  (maple-gammatone sr [lo hi fmax])
  the same with a gammatone envelope (sharp attack, slow decay): better on attacks
#maple-cut
  (maple-cut x sr mode [a b] [source])
  a dictionary of atoms cut from a sound: mode 'frames (Hann frames a ms long,
  every b ms; 100 100), 'onsets (the spans between onsets, threshold a, at most b ms; 2 1000) or 'whole (at most
  a ms; 2000). Each atom has unit energy and remembers its source (a name) and where it was cut
#maple-merge
  (maple-merge d1 d2 ...)
  one dictionary of the atoms of several (dictionaries of sounds at one rate)
#maple-info
  (maple-info d)
  a dictionary as a record: kind (gabor, gammatone, sounds), sr, size (atoms, or scales), and the
  windows (lo hi) and fmax of a parametric one
#maple-atom
  (maple-atom d k)
  atom k of a dictionary of sounds, a vector (unit energy), to listen to or plot
#maple-save
  (maple-save d path)
  a dictionary to a file; (maple-load path) one from a file (also those Moritz's atoms object writes)
#maple-load
  (maple-load path)
  a dictionary saved with maple-save
#maple-decompose
  (maple-decompose x sr d [opts])
  a sound explained by the atoms of d, the strongest first: a book. Options: 'atoms (2000)
  and 'snr (30 dB: stop when the residual is that far under the sound) for Gabor and gammatone; for sounds 'components
  (4 atoms a segment), 'candidates (16, by mel preselection), 'segments ('onsets or 'blocks), 'block (100 ms, the
  blocks or the longest segment), 'threshold (2, onsets). A sound at another rate than a dictionary of sounds is resampled
#maple-book
  (maple-book b)
  a book as 8 rows, one value per atom: time (s, the atom's centre), frequency (Hz), level (dB), atom
  (-1: Gabor or gammatone), length (samples), amplitude, phase, start (samples). (add-scatter fig (head b) (getidx b 1) "")
  draws the atom map
#maple-residual
  (maple-residual b)
  what the atoms of a book leave unexplained, a vector at the book's rate
#maple-snr
  (maple-snr b)
  how well a book explains its sound: the sound's energy over the residual's, in dB
#maple-rate
  (maple-rate b)
  the rate of a book (its dictionary's, for sounds)
#maple-synth
  (maple-synth b [opts] [d])
  the sound rebuilt from a book: options 'ratio (transposition, 1), 'stretch (time, 1), 'tails
  (1: sound atoms ring on whole; 0: only what matched), 'keep (the share of atoms, strongest first, 1). With another
  dictionary of sounds d, each atom is replaced by the closest of d: the sound made of the other's material (cross
  synthesis). Never above 0.99: louder results are scaled down
#soundtypes-analyse
  (soundtypes-analyse x sr [opts])
  a sound as types (SoundTypes): its frames (MFCCs, centroid, loudness) clustered into
  types, runs of one type the units of level 1; where the next type is surprising a gesture ends, and the gestures
  are clustered into the types of level 2, and so on. Options: 'types (list 12 6 4), 'levels (2, at most 3),
  'threshold (1: surprise above the mean plus 1 sd), 'smooth (5 frames), 'seed, 'size (2048), 'hop (512), 'segment
  ('frames, or 'onsets: level 1 the spans between onsets, 'onset-threshold 1.5 'onset-gap 0.08 s), 'pitch (1 adds
  the chroma: types follow harmony too)
#soundtypes-analyse-book
  (soundtypes-analyse-book b [opts])
  the same on the atoms of a pursuit book (maple-decompose): units are rebuilt
  from their atoms (the frames are those of the atoms; 'segment 'onsets needs a sound)
#soundtypes-levels
  (soundtypes-levels m)
  the number of units at each level, a list
#soundtypes-units
  (soundtypes-units m level)
  the units of a level (1, 2, 3), each (list start end type), in seconds
#soundtypes-labels
  (soundtypes-labels m)
  the type of every frame, a vector per level (one value per hop): plot them as images
#soundtypes-transitions
  (soundtypes-transitions m level)
  how often each type follows each other at a level: a matrix (row: from, column: to)
#soundtypes-generate
  (soundtypes-generate m level seconds [opts])
  a new sequence of the units of a level, made sound: (list sound units),
  the units' numbers in the order played. Options: 'method ('oracle: a factor oracle, continue the original with
  'continuity 0.8 or jump where the last 'context 1 units repeat; 'markov: the longest context seen 'min-count 2
  times, up to 'order; 'classic: n-grams of 'order 2), 'seed, 'xfade (10 ms), 'inner (1; under 1, each gesture of
  level 2 or 3 is played by new units of level 1 with that continuity, 'inner-context 1)
#soundtypes-match
  (soundtypes-match a b level [opts])
  SoundTypes' rematch: sound a rebuilt with the material of b. Level 0: frame by
  frame (b's frames overlap-added at a's); 1, 2...: unit by unit, each of a's replaced by the closest of b in its
  closest type. Options: 'fit (1: at a's times and durations; 0: one after the other), 'contour (0..1: a's loudness
  imposed on the result), 'space ('own: each sound's features in its own range; 'joint: one space), 'xfade (10 ms).
  Both models analysed the same way (both sounds, or both books); the result is at b's rate
#midi-read
  (midi-read path)
  => a record: ppq, seconds, tracks (names), and notes (records: track channel pitch velocity at dur),
  times in seconds after the file's tempo map
#render
  (render s "out.wav" "stereo")
  writes the mix;  layouts: "mono" "stereo" "binaural" "ambi N", a list of
  speaker azimuths (a ring), or a number of channels (multichannel events as they are)
#play-score
  (play-score s gain)
  plays it through live, ahead of the clock (synths compiled, the rest rendered),
  everything scaled by gain
#display
  (display s)
  the roll: rows by kind (notes in orchestral order, then files, buffers, synths,
  calls); WASD and + - 0 navigate in time, hovering shows an event and the time
#score
  (score name sr)
  a new, empty score at a sample rate
#score-tempo! score-bpm
  (score-tempo! s bpm)  (score-bpm s)
  the score's tempo, for times written in beats (60 by default: a beat is a second)
#beat->sec
  (beat->sec s b)
  a time in beats of the score as seconds
#score-reverb!
  (score-reverb! s dry wet)
  how much of the score is heard dry and through the hall when it is played (0.7 and 0.3
  by default; (score-reverb! s 1 0) plays it dry)
#score-events score-sr score-duration
  (score-events s)  (score-sr s)  (score-duration s)
  its events (in the order they were added), rate, end time
#event-end
  (event-end e)
  when the event ends
#event
  (event s at dur what)
  add an event; what is a path, a buffer, a note, an instrument, a call, or a function;
  => the event record (its at and dur can be changed later with put!)
#event-at
  (event-at s at dur what az el)
  the same, placed at an azimuth and an elevation (degrees, 0 in front, left positive)
#score-next-id!
  (score-next-id! s)
  a fresh event number: ids are never reused, even after events are removed (the roll and
  score-choose! find events by their id)
#payload->event
  (payload->event what)
  the event record of a payload (kind and source), without its time
#filename
  (filename path)
  the last part of a path, for labels
#event-gain!
  (event-gain! e g)
  the gain of an event (1 by default); (event-move! e at) (event-length! e dur) (event-place! e az el)
#instrument
  (instrument f params)
  a synth event: f a streamable instrument function (gate first), params its parameters
  as (list (list 'freq 440) ...); the gate is the event's duration
#call
  (call f args)
  a call event: f applied to args when the score is rendered; its result (a vector or a
  list of channels) is the sound. A function taking the duration can ask for it: pass
  'dur among the args, it is replaced by the event's duration in seconds
#fn-name
  (fn-name f)
  the name a function prints as, for labels
#load-sound
  (load-sound path)
  a WAV as (list sr channels), from the cache
#note-sound
  (note-sound e sr)
  a note's channels at a rate: the file's, shifted by resampling when the pitch was not
  the recording's; only what the event's duration needs is resampled (a little more for
  the fade), and the result is kept in the cache under file, shift, rate and length
#clear-sound-cache
  (clear-sound-cache)
  forget the loaded files and the notes made from them
#to-rate
  (to-rate channels from to)
  channels resampled from one rate to another (nothing to do when equal)
#render-event
  (render-event e sr)
  the sound of an event at the score's rate: a list of channels, cut to its duration
  with a fade at the end when the sound is longer, gain applied
#fit-duration
  (fit-duration x dur sr)
  x cut to dur seconds with a fade-out over the last 20 ms (or a quarter of dur), if longer
#layout-channels
  (layout-channels layout)
  how many channels a layout has
#place
  (place chans layout az el sr)
  an event's channels into the layout's channels: a mono sound is spatialised at its
  direction; a sound with as many channels as the layout goes in as it is; anything else is
  summed to mono first
#score-render
  (score-render s layout)
  the whole score as channels at its rate; a score placed as an event is rendered into the
  same layout (its own positions kept), cut to the event's duration with a fade
#render-buffer
  (render-buffer s layout)
  the score as channels, in the concert hall as the roll plays it (score-reverb!: the dry
  and wet amounts; (score-reverb! s 1 0) renders dry), scaled down when it would clip; the
  buffer to keep working on; (score-render s layout) is the dry mix itself
#render
  (render s path layout)
  render-buffer written as a WAV at the score's rate; => the channels
#render-hall
  (render-hall s path)
  the score in the hall, in stereo, as a WAV (the roll's Render... button): (render s path "stereo")
#play-score
  (play-score s gain)
  play the score now (the device is opened if needed) and wait until it ends or is stopped
  (stop-score); gain scales it, with the score's 'level (0.5 by default: many players at
  fff add up; the bus limiter catches the rest); the roll's cursor follows
#play-score-from
  (play-score-from s gain from)
  the same from a time in seconds
#bus-hall!
  (bus-hall! sr dry wet)
  the concert hall on the output bus at a rate and mix, set only when it changes (setting it
  again would cut the tail)
#score-play-now
  (score-play-now s gain from)
  start playing and return at once (what the roll's Play button does); => the end time on
  the clock. stop-score stops it.
#azimuth->pan
  (azimuth->pan az)
  an azimuth in degrees (0 in front, left positive) as the engine's pan, -1 (left) to 1 (right)
#score-flatten
  (score-flatten s depth)
  the score's events with those of the scores inside brought to the top: copies at absolute
  times, the gains multiplied, cut to their score's event; => a list
#score-hall-mix
  (score-hall-mix s sr)
  the score rendered in stereo and put in the hall, at a rate; kept in the score (its
  'cache) with a signature of the events, so playing again without a change is instant
#score-clear-cache!
  (score-clear-cache! s)
  forget the rendered mix (an event's sound changed in a way the signature cannot see)
#stop-score
  (stop-score)
  stop whatever score is playing, at once
#score-render-at
  (score-render-at s layout sr)
  the score rendered at a rate other than its own (the device's, when playing)
#score-schedule
  (score-schedule s gain from)
  the live way: every event scheduled on the clock (synths compiled and gated, the rest
  rendered), no hall; returns at once => (list synth-ids end-clock-time start-clock-time);
  free the synths when it is over
#instrument-rank
  (instrument-rank instr)
  where an instrument code sits in the orchestral order (unknown ones after)
#score-rows
  (score-rows s)
  the rows of the roll: one per instrument (orchestral order) for the notes, then one
  per kind: files, buffers, synths, calls; => (list (list label events) ...)
#roll-events
  (roll-events s)
  the events as the roll shows them: a chord becomes one note per pitch (same id and time)
#score-roll
  (score-roll s)
  the roll as a figure: rows (name and clef) and bars (row start dur label tip group lane lanes
  midi dyn id tech cents); pitched events sit on their row's staff, the others on a line;
  the technique is written above a note where it changes, the tuning in cents when not zero
#register-score
  (register-score s)
  remember a score under a number (the roll carries it); => the number
#displayed-score
  (displayed-score id)
  the score registered under a number
#roll-play
  (roll-play score-id from)
  start a displayed score from a time (the roll's Play button); (roll-stop) stops it;
  (roll-render score-id path) the score in the hall as a WAV (the roll's Render button)
#roll-save
  (roll-save score-id path)
  the score's notes as a connection file (the roll's Save button; score-save)
#roll-choose
  (roll-choose score-id orch seg n)
  solution n of segment seg of the orch-th orchestration in a displayed score (the
  roll's solution menu): the score's notes replaced (score-choose!) and the roll redrawn
#play-event
  (play-event score-id event-id)
  play one event of a displayed score, alone (a double-click in the roll does this)
#event-lanes
  (event-lanes events)
  a lane number per event such that events sharing a lane do not overlap in time
#display
  (display s)
  show the score as a roll: a staff per instrument with note heads and duration lines, a
  line per other kind; A D pan and + - zoom in time, W S scroll and Z X zoom the rows,
  R resets; hovering shows an event; a double-click plays it; Play (or Space) plays the
  score from the cursor (a click in the background places it), Stop stops; the cursor
  follows any play-score; in a build without windows it does nothing
#db-load
  (db-load path)
  load a database from its feature file: TinySOL.spectrum.db with the sounds in TinySOL/ next
  to it (the paths in the file are relative to that folder); when no such folder exists the
  sounds are looked for next to the file itself. => a record with 'path, 'root (the sounds'
  folder), 'type, 'block, 'hop, 'ncoeff and 'entries (records: file instr tech pitch dyn
  other midi features). The sounds are not read: notes open them when rendered or played.
#db-load-first
  (db-load-first paths)
  load the first database of a list that is on disk: the examples name the set they prefer
  first (TinySOL, FullSOL) and the bundled MicroSOL last, and run with what is there
#db-sounds-folder
  (db-sounds-folder dir entries)
  where the sounds of a feature file in dir are: the folder next to it (or dir itself)
  under which the first entry's file exists, whatever the folder is called (TinySOL/, tinysol/,
  a copy named otherwise); dir when nothing is found (a note then says the sound is missing)
#db-merge
  (db-merge dbs)
  one database out of a list of several, when their features agree (same type and number of
  coefficients): the entries of all, each remembering its own sounds' folder; a note
  then draws on every set at once. (db-load (list "a.db" "b.db")) is the same.
#db-size db-instruments db-techniques db-dynamics db-pitches
  (db-size db)  (db-instruments db)  (db-techniques db)  (db-dynamics db)  (db-pitches db)
  what the database holds
#db-query
  (db-query db instr pitch dyn tech)
  the entries matching the given values; nil matches anything, a list matches
  any of its members: (db-query db 'Vn nil 'mf nil) every mf violin sound,
  (db-query db (list 'Vn 'Va) nil (list 'pp 'p) 'ord) quiet upper strings
#db-grep
  (db-grep db pattern)
  the entries whose file name matches a regular expression: (db-grep db "Fl-ord-C.-pp")
#db-find
  (db-find db text)
  the entries whose file name contains the text: (db-find db "Vn-ord-C5")
#db-between
  (db-between db instr lo hi)
  the entries of an instrument between two pitches (names or MIDI numbers), inclusive
#db-nearest
  (db-nearest db entry n)
  the n entries whose features are closest (euclidean) to an entry's: sounds alike
#db-available
  (db-available db)
  the entries whose sounds are on disk; (db-instruments-available db) their instruments
#db-techniques-of
  (db-techniques-of db instr)
  the techniques an instrument was recorded with (on disk); (db-dynamics-of db instr) its dynamics
#db-range
  (db-range db instr)
  the lowest and highest MIDI note of an instrument, as (list lo hi)
#db-range-available
  (db-range-available db instr)
  the range of the sounds actually on disk, from the index (fast; what the
  orchestrators use)
#db-path
  (db-path db entry)
  the sound file of an entry, on disk: under the sounds' folder at the path the feature file
  gives when it exists, else found by its file name anywhere under that folder (the folders
  of a copy may be named otherwise, and a sharp written # in the file may be _ on disk);
  the path as the file gives it when the sound is not there at all
#db-available?
  (db-available? db entry)
  is the sound file of an entry on disk? (a feature file may describe more sounds than are present)
#db-features
  (db-features entry)
  the feature vector of an entry
#db-make
  (db-make folder path type block hop ncoeff)
  analyse every WAV under a folder into a feature file (db-gen) and load it
#db-index!
  (db-index! db)
  builds (if not yet) the index: for every instrument, its available pitched entries,
  grouped by dynamics and technique; note and db-range read it, so a large database
  (FullSOL has tens of thousands of entries) costs a scan once, not per note
#db-candidates
  (db-candidates db instr dyn tech)
  the available pitched entries of an instrument with these dynamics and
  technique; failing that, with the technique; failing that, any of the instrument
#note
  (note db instr pitch dyn tech)
  a note event (pitch a name, "D#5", or a MIDI number): the entry matching instrument, pitch, dynamics and technique, or
  the nearest available pitch of that instrument (same dynamics and technique when they
  exist), shifted by resampling to the pitch asked for. Only entries whose sound is on
  disk are candidates.
#note-cents!
  (note-cents! n cents)
  a note's tuning away from its pitch, in cents (shown in the roll; used by the orchestrators
  that know the target's exact frequencies); the shift by resampling follows it
#note-path
  (note-path e)
  the sound file of a note event, on disk
#note-duration
  (note-duration e)
  how long the note's sound is, in seconds (after the shift)
#pitch->name
  (pitch->name p)
  a pitch as a name, whatever was given
#pitch->number
  (pitch->number p)
  a pitch as a MIDI number
#rhythm
  (rhythm d ...)
  durations in seconds; negative ones are pauses: (rhythm 0.5 0.5 -0.25 1)
#beats
  (beats bpm r)
  a rhythm given in beats, at a tempo
#rhythm-duration
  (rhythm-duration r)
  how long a rhythm lasts (pauses count)
#chord
  (chord db instr dyn tech pitches)
  a chord payload: the pitches sounding together on one instrument (as many
  notes, each resolved by note); place it with event, or in a fragment
#notes
  (notes db instr dyn tech pitches rhythm)
  a line: the pitches one after another with the rhythm's durations; the
  shorter of the two repeats until the longer ends; => a fragment
#chords
  (chords db instr dyn tech chord-list rhythm)
  chords (lists of pitches) one after another, with the rhythm
#line-of
  (line-of items rhythm maker)
  the shared engine of notes and chords: items and durations cycled to the longer, maker
  turns an item into a payload (nil items and negative durations are rests)
#fragment-duration fragment-shift fragment-scale fragment-map
  (fragment-duration f)  (fragment-shift f dt)  (fragment-scale f k)  (fragment-map f g)
  fragments as data: their length,
  moved in time, stretched (times and durations by k), or every (at dur payload) triple through g
#fragment-repeat
  (fragment-repeat f times)
  the fragment played times in a row
#fragment-until
  (fragment-until f secs)
  the fragment repeated until secs (the last events cut off), for textures
#add!
  (add! s at fragment)
  place a fragment's events into a score at a time; => the events
#fragment->score
  (fragment->score name sr fragment)
  a score of its own, to place inside another with event
#texture
  (texture db instrs dyn tech pitches rhythm scales)
  micropolyphony: one voice per scale factor, each the same line
  with the rhythm multiplied by its factor, every voice repeating its line until the slowest
  has played it once; instruments cycled over the voices; => a fragment
#pivots
  (pivots db instrs dyn tech chord interval rhythm)
  as many lines as the chord has pitches, each wandering at random
  within +- interval semitones of its pitch, one note per duration of the rhythm; => a fragment
#chordinterp
  (chordinterp db instr dyn tech chord1 chord2 rhythm)
  from one chord to another in as many steps as the rhythm has
  durations, each voice moving by rounded semitone steps (the shorter chord's voices held); => a fragment
#transpose-pitches
  (transpose-pitches pitches n)
  pitches n semitones higher (rests kept); (invert pitches axis) mirrored around a pitch
#scale-pitches
  (scale-pitches root mode degrees)
  pitches of a scale: root a pitch, mode 'major 'minor 'dorian 'phrygian 'lydian
  'mixolydian 'aeolian 'locrian 'chromatic 'whole 'pentatonic, degrees a list of scale steps (0 = root)
#add-beats!
  (add-beats! s beat fragment)
  a fragment whose times are in beats, placed at a beat of the score (its tempo)
#fragment-gain
  (fragment-gain f from to)
  the events' gains ramped from one value to another along the fragment (a crescendo)
#fragment-dynamics
  (fragment-dynamics db f dyns)
  the notes of a fragment re-resolved with dynamics stepping through a list along it
#fragment-articulate
  (fragment-articulate f fraction)
  every event sounding for a fraction of its duration (staccato at 0.3)
#fragment-thin
  (fragment-thin f p)
  each event kept with probability p
#fragment-density
  (fragment-density f curve)
  events kept with a probability read along the fragment from a curve (a list, 0..1)
#fragment-place
  (fragment-place f az el)
  the events placed at a direction (kept when added with add!)
#fragment-snap
  (fragment-snap f field)
  the notes snapped to the nearest pitch of a field (a list of pitches), re-resolved
#snap-to-field
  (snap-to-field p field)
  the pitch of the field nearest to p
#pitch-field
  (pitch-field root mode octaves)
  every pitch of a scale over some octaves from the root, as a field to snap to
#chord-voicing
  (chord-voicing pitches mode)
  a chord revoiced: 'close (as given, sorted), 'open (every other voice up an octave),
  'drop2 (the second from the top down an octave), 'spread (each voice an octave above the
  previous), (list 'invert n) (n inversions: the lowest voices up an octave)
#rotate retrograde cycle interleave
  (rotate L n)  (retrograde L)  (cycle L n)  (interleave a b)
  series as lists: turned by n, backwards, n elements round and round, alternated
#pitches-from-spectrum
  (pitches-from-spectrum x sr n)
  the n strongest partials of a sound as MIDI pitches, low to high: a chord from a
  spectrum, the way spectral music builds one (a harmonic sound gives its harmonic series)
#harmonic-series
  (harmonic-series fundamental n)
  the first n partials of a fundamental (a pitch) as MIDI pitches, rounded
#just-cents
  (just-cents fundamental pitch n)
  the cents a tempered pitch is away from the nearest of the first n partials of a
  fundamental (a just overtone chord: the 7th partial -31, the 11th -49, the 13th +41, the
  14th -31 cents); nil when the pitch is not one of them (within a quarter tone)
#rhythm-from-pattern
  (rhythm-from-pattern "x..x.x" step)
  a rhythm from a string: x an attack, . a continuation of the step, each step lasting step seconds
#rhythm-augment rhythm-diminish
  (rhythm-augment r k)  (rhythm-diminish r k)
  every duration multiplied, divided by k
#tuplet
  (tuplet n total)
  n equal durations filling total seconds (a triplet: (tuplet 3 1))
#polyrhythm
  (polyrhythm ra rb)
  the two rhythms extended to a common length (each repeated), => (list ra' rb')
#walk
  (walk db instrs dyn tech starts step-max rhythm)
  random walks: one line per start pitch, each note within step-max
  semitones of the previous one (pivots stay near a centre; a walk drifts)
#texture-staggered
  (texture-staggered db instrs dyn tech pitches rhythm scales entries)
  a texture whose voices enter one after another
  (entries: a delay in seconds per voice), each repeating until the last has played once
#arpeggio
  (arpeggio db instr dyn tech pitches spread mode dur)
  the chord's notes one after another spread seconds apart,
  'up 'down 'updown or 'random, each held for dur; => a fragment
#chordinterp-ease
  (chordinterp-ease db instr dyn tech c1 c2 rhythm exponent)
  chord interpolation with a curve: exponent 1 linear, > 1
  slow then fast, < 1 fast then slow
#chordinterp-sets
  (chordinterp-sets db instr dyn tech c1 c2 rhythm)
  interpolation between pitch sets: every voice of the first
  chord goes to the nearest free pitch of the second (no crossing by index), then as chordinterp
#texture-on-chords
  (texture-on-chords db instrs dyn tech chord-list rhythm scales)
  a texture whose line runs through the chords in
  turn (each chord's pitches, then the next), so the micropolyphony moves from one harmony to
  another: the chord list can come from chordinterp's chords
#texture-on-pivots
  (texture-on-pivots db instrs dyn tech chord interval rhythm scales)
  the pivots' lines taken as a texture: every
  voice wanders around its chord pitch at its own speed
#orchestrate-line
  (orchestrate-line db line rhythm registers dyn tech)
  a line distributed over instruments by register: registers a
  list of (list instr lo hi); each pitch goes to the first instrument whose range holds it
#score-map!
  (score-map! s f)
  every event through f (a function of the event record, returning a record), in place
#score-instrument
  (score-instrument s instr)
  the events of an instrument
#midi->fragment
  (midi->fragment path db instr tech)
  the notes of a MIDI file as a fragment on one instrument, velocities
  becoming dynamics (pp p mp mf f ff over 0..127); times as the file's tempo map says
#midi->fragment-by-channel
  (midi->fragment-by-channel path db instrs tech)
  the same with an instrument per MIDI channel (instrs a list; a
  channel beyond the list takes the last one), => one fragment
#velocity->dynamics
  (velocity->dynamics v)
  a MIDI velocity as one of pp p mp mf f ff
#midi->score
  (midi->score path db instrs tech name)
  a score from a MIDI file, an instrument per channel
#orchestration
  (orchestration method params segments)
  a result record
#segment
  (segment at dur solutions)
  a segment: solutions a list of (list cost fragment), best first
#solutions
  (solutions result k)
  the solutions of segment k, best first, as (list cost fragment) pairs
#solution
  (solution result k n)
  the fragment of the n-th solution of segment k
#connection
  (connection result choices)
  one solution per segment (choices: an index per segment) joined into a fragment; a
  note that continues across a boundary on the same instrument at the same pitch is merged
#best-connection
  (best-connection result)
  the first solution of every segment
#connect!
  (connect! s at result choices)
  a connection placed in a score; the score remembers the orchestration, so that the
  roll (or score-choose!) can put another solution of a segment in its place
#score-choose!
  (score-choose! s k seg n)
  in the k-th orchestration connected into the score (connect!, in order), solution n of
  segment seg in place of the one chosen: its notes replaced; => the new events
#score-solutions
  (score-solutions s)
  the orchestrations connected into a score, with their segments and the solution chosen in
  each: a list of (list at (list (list seg-at seg-dur chosen costs) ...)); what the roll shows
#merge-continuations
  (merge-continuations f)
  in a fragment, a note starting where a note of the same instrument and pitch ends becomes
  the continuation of that note (one longer event), as an orchestration's connection does;
  notes that carry their 'player (the granulator's do) merge only with the same player's
#merge-continuations-within
  (merge-continuations-within f hold)
  the same, a continued note never longer than hold seconds: a player who
  cannot hold a note that long (an oboe without a breath) starts it again instead
#env
  (env t0 v0 t1 v1 ...)
  a value changing with time: at each breakpoint a value; between breakpoints a number or
  a range (list lo hi) is interpolated, and a set (a list of symbols, pitches or chords) is
  crossfaded: nearer the earlier breakpoint the earlier set is drawn more often. Given as a
  flat list: (env (list 0 (list 1 2) 10 (list 0.1 0.2)))
#env-at
  (env-at e t)
  the value at time t: an interpolated number or range, or a set chosen by the crossfade
#draw-in
  (draw-in range)
  a random number in a range (or the number itself)
#pick-from
  (pick-from set)
  a random element of a set (or the value itself when it is not a list of alternatives)
#dynamics-level?
  (dynamics-level? v)
  is a dynamics parameter a level (a number or a range) rather than a set of labels?
#level->dynamics
  (level->dynamics x)
  a level 0..1 as the nearest label of ppp pp p mp mf f ff fff; (dynamics->level d) the reverse
#level->gain
  (level->gain x)
  a level as a gain, 0.25 at ppp to 1 at fff (the sample carries the timbre of its dynamics,
  the gain the finer steps between the recorded ones)
#orchestra
  (orchestra spec)
  the players: spec a list where a symbol is one player of that instrument, a string with
  | is one player alternating between instruments (an ossia: "Fl|Picc"), and a list is a
  group of players scheduled together (paired): (orchestra (list 'Fl 'Fl "Ob|EH" (list 'Vn 'Vc)))
  => a list of player records: instrs, group, and the state the granulator keeps for each
  (busy-until, last-pitch, last-tech, seat)
#orchestra-rest!
  (orchestra-rest! orch)
  every player free again and its memory cleared (the last pitch, the technique, the seat):
  for a run of granulators that share one orchestra ('continue) when a new piece begins
#orchestra-size
  (orchestra-size orch)
  how many players; (orchestra-instruments orch) every instrument they can play
#orchestra-range
  (orchestra-range db orch)
  the lowest and highest MIDI pitch any instrument of the orchestra was recorded at (on disk);
  (orchestra-octaves db orch) the same as octaves, the granulator's register unit: what to clip a
  band taken from a recording to, so that it asks nothing the orchestra cannot play
#instrument-family
  (instrument-family instr)
  'winds 'brass 'percussion 'keyboard 'plucked or 'strings by the instrument code (the
  orchestral order); 'other for a code it does not know. What a 'balance may be given by
#balance-gain
  (balance-gain balance instr)
  the gain of an instrument under a 'balance: a record from instrument codes or families
  to decibels, (record (list 'brass -6 'Hn -3)): the instrument's own entry, else its family's,
  else 0 dB; => a linear gain
#orchestrate-granular
  (orchestrate-granular db orch secs params)
  orchestration as granular synthesis: a stochastic process realised by
  the players of an orchestra, never more at once than there are players, each event a note that a player of the
  orchestra can play as recorded (the pitch, the technique, and with 'dynamics-strict the dynamics, are those of a
  sample of the instrument: the constraints select and are never relaxed; what no player can play is reported and
